title: Strong Converse for Quantum Capacity via a Fully Quantum Blowing-Up Lemma
abstract: We prove an exponential strong converse for quantum communication through every finite-dimensional memoryless channel: at any fixed rate above the quantum capacity, the entanglement-transmission fidelity of every code decays exponentially with the number of channel uses. The proof has two main ingredients. First, a fully quantum blowing-up lemma converts a low-fidelity code into a high-fidelity code, with a loss in the number of transmitted qubits controlled by the projective tensor norm of the orthogonal projection on the image of the Stinespring dilation of the channel across the receiver--environment bipartition. Second, a low-degree polynomial construction approximates the tensor power of this projector with exponential accuracy while controlling its projective norm, providing the approximation needed for the blowing-up argument.

bite.hook: Transmitting above quantum capacity causes fidelity to decay exponentially for all memoryless channels.
tldr: Proved an exponential strong converse theorem for quantum capacity across all finite-dimensional memoryless channels.
Developed a fully quantum blowing-up lemma to turn low-fidelity codes into high-fidelity ones.
Constructed low-degree polynomial approximations of channel Stinespring projector powers with bounded projective norms.
bite.whyItMatters: Shannon proved that classical data sent faster than channel capacity turns to complete gibberish; this proof confirms the exact same sharp, exponential breakdown holds for quantum communication, cementing a foundational limit of quantum networks.
bite.eli5: If you try to stream video faster than your internet pipe allows, a few glitches might seem tolerable, but this theorem proves that once you pass the quantum speed limit, the signal instantly and completely collapses into static.

glossary.shortDef: A property stating that exceeding channel capacity causes transmission success probability to vanish asymptotically.
glossary.eli5Def: A guarantee that going even slightly over the speed limit doesn't just degrade performance—it causes total failure.
